claim: Blocking Slackbot in robots.txt prevents Slack previews.
reality: Slack does not honor robots.txt for link unfurling.

claim: Mixed images make Google prefer the HTTP version of the page.
reality: Google's canonicalization exception covers 'insecure dependencies (other than images)'. Passive images are auto-upgraded by Chrome.
patterns: mixed images make google prefer http
mixed images cause an http canonical

claim: Small fonts and tiny tap targets are Google ranking or indexing problems.
reality: These are UX and accessibility checks. The Google report that showed them is retired, and Lighthouse moved them out of SEO (target-size is now an a11y audit, and font-size was removed).
patterns: tap targets are a ranking factor
font size is a ranking factor
small fonts are a ranking factor

claim: Blocking Google-Extended removes a site from AI Overviews or AI Mode.
reality: Google-Extended controls Gemini model training and grounding in Gemini Apps and Vertex AI. It does not affect inclusion or ranking in Google Search. The AI features are controlled with nosnippet, max-snippet, noindex or the site-wide Search Console generative AI control.
patterns: block google-extended to opt out of ai overviews
block google-extended to stay out of ai
use google-extended to opt out of ai overviews

claim: Blocking GPTBot removes the site from ChatGPT search.
reality: GPTBot is for training. ChatGPT search inclusion is controlled by OAI-SearchBot, and OpenAI says each setting is independent.
patterns: allow gptbot to appear in chatgpt search
block gptbot to opt out of chatgpt search

claim: Content must be chunked into small passages or rewritten specially for AI.
reality: Google: there is no requirement to break content into tiny pieces, no ideal page length, and no need to write in a specific way for generative AI search.
patterns: break content into small chunks for ai

claim: Seeding brand mentions across the web is a reliable AI-visibility tactic.
reality: Google: seeking inauthentic mentions is not as helpful as it might seem, and its spam systems target manipulation of generative AI responses. Studies show AI engines favour earned third-party coverage, which is not the same as manufactured mentions.
patterns: post brand mentions on reddit for ai
get mentioned on reddit for ai

claim: GEO tactics (adding quotes and statistics) reliably boost AI citations by 40%.
reality: The up-to-40% figure is from lab conditions on GEO-bench, with gains concentrated on lower-ranked sources and losses for top-ranked ones. C-SEO Bench (NeurIPS D&B 2025) found most such methods largely ineffective and classic ranking much more effective.
patterns: add statistics to boost ai citations by

claim: Keyword stuffing helps LLM answers pick your page.
reality: In the GEO paper, keyword stuffing lowered position-adjusted visibility (about -8%) and was the worst method tested.

claim: All AI crawlers render JavaScript like Googlebot.
reality: In Vercel/MERJ's network measurement, GPTBot, ClaudeBot and PerplexityBot fetched JS files but did not execute them. Googlebot (used for Gemini) and Applebot render.

claim: robots.txt blocks every AI fetch, including those made for a user.
reality: User-triggered fetchers from Google, Perplexity and OpenAI generally ignore robots.txt or may not apply it; Meta's fetcher may bypass it. Anthropic's Claude-User is an exception that honours robots.txt.

claim: Content-Signal lines (ai-train=no, ai-input=no) are enforced and legally block AI use.
reality: Cloudflare describes them as preferences, not technical countermeasures, and says some companies may ignore them. No major operator has stated that it honours them.

claim: Third-party AI visibility tools show your real Google AI Overview rankings.
reality: Google: no third-party tool has access to its internal ranking or AI systems. First-party data is the Search Console Generative AI performance report (impressions only).
patterns: ai visibility tools show your real

claim: Opting out of Google's AI features hurts your regular rankings.
reality: Google says the Search Console generative AI control is not used as a ranking signal for results outside those features. The site loses AI-feature traffic and impressions only.
patterns: opting out of ai features hurts rankings
opting out of ai overviews hurts rankings

claim: Ranking in the top 10 guarantees an AI Overview citation, or only top-10 pages get cited.
reality: Ahrefs found 76% of cited pages in the top 10 (Jul 2025), and its later 2026 data, with a changed methodology, about 38%. Correlation is moderate and many citations come from deeper results. (Industry studies; the 2026 figure comes from secondary coverage.)
patterns: rank in the top 10 to be cited

claim: Applebot-Extended must be allowed for Siri/Spotlight visibility.
reality: Applebot-Extended does not crawl; it only controls training use of data Applebot already crawled, and is not considered in search ranking. Applebot is the crawler to allow.
patterns: allow applebot-extended to appear in siri

claim: Blocking AI crawler IP addresses is a reliable opt-out.
reality: Anthropic says IP blocking may not work correctly or persistently. Cloudflare documented undeclared crawling from rotating IPs. robots.txt plus verified-bot WAF rules are the documented path.
patterns: use ip blocking to opt out of ai

claim: Setting every sitemap lastmod to today signals freshness to AI search.
reality: Bing: lastmod must reflect the real content change, not the sitemap generation time. Google: page dates must describe actual publication or update.
patterns: set all lastmod values to today
set lastmod to the current date
